seen_animation: A close-up of a line-drawn cow head (polygonal ears, dash eyes, a wide rounded snout), with a grey cloud at upper left, a grey horizon line at left and a grey X mark at right. In frame 1 the head is tilted clockwise, with the snout low and to the right and the left cheek line hanging loose. By frame 2 the head has rotated most of the way upright, and by frame 3 it is upright and centred. It then holds that pose for frames 3-16 while the mouth changes: a closed smile in 1-3, a small open trapezoid in 4, open in 5-7, wider in 8, open in 9, closed smile in 10, open in 11, wide in 12, open in 13, closed in 14, and wide in 15-16. A body spot (an oval) and the back line of the body sit to the right of the head. A small hook mark at the bottom right is the top of a leg.
seen_film: A live-action close-up of a brown cow with a white blaze, against a sky and a dark horizon. In frame 1 the head is tilted and turned, with the muzzle low and to the right. By frame 2 the head is nearly upright, and by frame 3 it is upright and facing the camera. From frames 3-16 the head stays frontal while the cow chews or moos: the mouth is slightly open in 4, open in 5-7, wide in 8, open in 9, nearly closed in 10, open in 11, wide in 12, open in 13, nearly closed in 14, open in 15 and wide in 16.
named_subject: A cow (head and front of body), seen face-on.
evidence: Frames 1-3: both the animation and the film show the head tilted with the muzzle to the lower right in frame 1, mostly upright in frame 2 and fully frontal in frame 3, with the head in the same place in the frame. Frames 4-16: the mouth cycle matches the film frame for frame. Wide openings fall in 8, 12 and 16 in both. Near-closed mouths fall in 10 and 14 in both. Mid openings fall in 5-7, 9, 11 and 13 in both. The only mismatch is frame 15, where the animation's mouth is wide and the film's is a mid opening. The head outline, ears and eyes keep the same strokes from frame 3 to frame 16, with no redraw. Small flaws: in frame 14 the closed mouth is drawn as a doubled, thickened stroke. Between frames 1 and 3 the body spot at right changes shape from a hook to a spiral to an oval. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The body spot to the right of the head changes construction across frames 1-3 (a broken hook in frame 1, a spiral in frame 2, a closed oval from frame 3 on), so it pops instead of moving with the head turn.
closes_when: The spot is the same closed oval in frames 1-3, only shifting and rotating with the head and body, and the frame 14 mouth is a single stroke like the closed mouth in frame 10.
protect: The frame 1-3 head turn timed to the film; the chew cycle with wide openings on 8, 12 and 16 and closures on 10 and 14; the stable head, ears and dash eyes from frame 3 on; the doodle's polygonal ears, dash eyes, wide flat-topped snout and open-ended strokes; the framing that places the head where the film's head is.
identity_gap: The head matches the doodle's construction (ear loops, two dash eyes, wide snout with a cross line, open stroke ends); the open trapezoid mouth is an addition, but it is drawn in the same straight-segment habit, and the body is mostly cropped out by the close framing.
